title: The 100 Girlfriends Who Really Love You (Hyakkano) Season 3 Reveals Key Visual With 17 Girls, July 5 Premiere
content: The 100 Girlfriends Who Really Love You (Hyakkano) Season 3 revealed a key visual, along with a July 5, 2026 premiere date. Studio Bibury Animation Studios is again in charge of the animation, with Hikaru Sato returning to direct. The new visual features 17 girlfriends, and you can check it out below.
author: Anime Corner

title: A Livid Lady's Guide to Getting Even Anime Unveils New Key Visual, Additional Cast, Theme Songs
content: The previously announced A Livid Lady’s Guide to Getting Even: How I Crushed My Homeland with My Mighty Grimoires anime unveiled a new key visual along with three additional cast members and the opening and ending theme songs. The anime is scheduled to premiere in July 2026.
author: Anime Corner

title: NIPPON SANGOKU Reveals Episode 5 Preview
content: NIPPON SANGOKU revealed the preview images and synopsis for Episode 5, which is set to premiere on Sunday, May 2. Studio Kafka is in charge of the animation. The anime is co-produced with Amazon MGM Studios and is currently streaming weekly on Prime Video.
author: Anime Corner

title: The World's Strongest Witch Gets Anime
content: The World’s Strongest Witch light novel by Sakaki Mochimaru is getting an anime adaptation. A teaser visual and announcement trailer were also released along with the main staff and cast. The anime is slated to release in October 2026. The anime stars Azusa Tachibana as the titular character Lorna.
author: Anime Corner

title: Young Ladies Don't Play Fighting Games Reveals New Trailer, July 7 Premiere
content: Young Ladies Don’t Play Fighting Games anime revealed a new trailer and a July 7 premiere date. The trailer also features the opening theme song “Inochi Mijikashi Tai Suru Otome yo!” by Hanabie. The anime was supposed to premiere in 2025 but was delayed .

title: My Hero Academia Is All Set For Its True Finale With First Look At Beloved Characters After 8 Years
content: In December 2025, fans bid a bittersweet farewell to My Hero Academia ‘s anime nine years after its debut. It took the anime series a little more than a year after the manga finale to wrap up the story with an epilogue of the Final War.
